title: Support Triage & De-escalation
description: Prioritise incoming tickets and calm frustrated customers. Tests empathy, issue categorisation, and conflict resolution.

seo.overviewTitle: Customer Support Triage & Angry Customer De-Escalation
seo.overviewBody: Frontline support operations determine customer retention and brand reputation. Support leads evaluate candidates on applying the HEAR de-escalation framework (Hear, Empathize, Apologize, Resolve), triaging ticket priority levels (P1 critical vs P4 minor), writing macro response templates, and recovering negative CSAT ratings.

deliverables.title: 1. De-Escalation & Angry Customer Playbook
deliverables.desc: Response guide detailing phrasing scripts, empathy statements, and escalation boundaries for handling frustrated users.

deliverables.title: 2. Ticket Triage & Severity Matrix (P1-P4)
deliverables.desc: Operational matrix classifying ticket urgency, response SLAs, and routing rules based on business impact.

deliverables.title: 3. CSAT Recovery Workflow Document
deliverables.desc: Standardized workflow for following up on negative CSAT ratings (1-2 stars) and resolving root cause complaints.

faqs.question: What is the HEAR framework in customer support de-escalation?
faqs.answer: HEAR stands for Hear (actively listen without interrupting), Empathize (validate their frustration), Apologize (own the experience sincerely without defensive excuses), and Resolve (provide clear, actionable next steps).

faqs.question: When should a customer support ticket be escalated to management?
faqs.answer: Escalate when a issue involves legal threats, executive complaints, severe financial loss, security data breaches, or when standard agent authority cannot resolve the customer's policy request.

faqs.question: How do you recover a negative Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) rating?
faqs.answer: Reach out within 24 hours via phone or personalized email, acknowledge the initial service breakdown, offer an immediate resolution or gesture of goodwill, and confirm satisfaction.
